paragraph: Single-family is the market in Washington Township, with 35 sales over six months at a median of $850,000 against a median list of $789,000. That is a sale-to-list ratio of 1.09, roughly 71 percent of homes closing above asking, and a median of 14 days on market. This is a real seller's market, and multiple offer situations are common at this price point. The range runs from $540,000 to $1,710,000, so the median is the better guide than either end. Condos and townhouses are a much thinner slice at 10 sales and a median of $730,000, moving in about 17 days with 80 percent going above list. The gap between the two tiers is narrow here, so a townhouse is not the entry-level option some buyers expect it to be. Monthly counts are small enough that any single month is noise, but the direction has been upward from February through July, which tracks the normal spring build into summer. If the usual seasonal arc holds, expect medians to ease as fall closings come through. If you're weighing tiers, the deciding factor isn't market heat. It's whether you want the space and grounds of a single-family or the low-maintenance lifestyle of a townhouse.
